scope_note: SG-MA-PHARMACIST-ADMINISTRATION after corrections following the V10J audit. Circular Letter DCP 26-03-124's sentence that the pharmacist or intern remains responsible for reporting a dispensing error or serious adverse drug event to the Board is kept as Department guidance in its own words, and beside it the section now teaches who files and what is reportable: under 247 CMR 20.02(1) and (2) the pharmacy's Manager of Record reports improper dispensing that results in serious injury or death, and a serious adverse drug event from a drug manufactured, produced or compounded at the pharmacy (to the Board, FDA MedWatch and the Betsy Lehman Center), each within seven business days from the event the rule names; under M.G.L. c. 112, s. 39D(b) the pharmacy informs the Department of Public Health of improper dispensing, and under s. 39D(c) the manager of record reports the serious adverse drug event. Neither text names the person who administered. Changed: orientation[8], comparison_tables[5] and [6], worked_examples[4], retrieval_prompts[24] and a new [25], quick_review[17] and a new [18], decision_logic[12] and a new [13], exceptions, timing_deadlines, forms_records[9], role_duties[9] with new Manager of Record and pharmacy entries, common_traps[20] with two new traps, learning objective 8 and the subtopic. forms_records[11] now limits the list's supply of the 105 CMR 700.004(B)(9)(d)1. drugs to its mental health and substance use disorder categories. New rule: MA-SERIOUS-EVENT-REPORTERS-AND-TRIGGERS; the vaguer MA-SERIOUS-EVENT-REPORT is not cited. Scope gate: 13 actionable signals declined; they are collaborative drug therapy management prescribing records (MA-CDTM-*), MA-PHARMACIST-PRESCRIBER-ID, and contraception and expedited partner therapy records (MA-HORMONAL-CONTRACEPTIVE, MA-CONTRACEPTION-PRESCRIBING-REGULATION, MA-EPT-PRACTITIONER-AUTHORITY), all concerning prescribing rather than administration and taught or planned in other sections. All six practice links stay.
